lines.text: Accepting you'll never say nor ever feel, my love was real.
What isn't mine I still cannot give.
I gather my things to go.
Before I go, we look at the moon the way we used to see it
and settle down the stillnessism.
We talk for years and travel through time
and it feels so good.
We grow old together.
I believe maybe we could have it all,
or swing in my humbled late nights and heartbreaks
and an end story unchanging.
You help me gather my things to go.
Before I go, I call on my mother.
In tears, speaking of an abyss, she's never known.
And we talk for years and we closet wounds
and we explain my way of birth then and even after prayer.
What isn't mine I still cannot give.
We grow old together with the moon looking at us
the way we used to be.
As my tears fall between the creases and faith,
dancing on my own, maternal ears in tune.
She watches us gather my things to go.
Before I go, I call on my father.
Summon his calming demeanor from the yonders
and we walk for years and travel east toward the sunrises
and retrace his footsteps now and then.
Guiding a settling down moon the way it used to leave
and my tears fall between the creases
and wave shadows of the inner harbor.
We stroll, father and son, hearted and shaken.
Someone borrowed and someone blew.
Yet broken, yet hurt.

characters.who: THE POET, a man: a Black man in his thirties, dark brown skin, short faded haircut, full well-groomed beard, as in the reference photos. He is the speaker of every poem.

characters.name: EX
characters.who: THE EX, a man the poet loved. His FACE IS NEVER SEEN: paint him only from behind and three-quarter behind; the head is the back of the head (short dark hair, the nape, one ear at most). Broad shoulders, slightly taller than the poet.

characters.name: THE WOMAN (was "the poet" puppet)
characters.who: THE WOMAN, the puppet the arena used to call 'the poet' (renamed: the poet is now the man). A Black woman, dark brown skin, a full rounded afro, eyes OPEN. In the poems she plays the women: the MOTHER (09), SHE in the far window (13).

characters.name: PARENTS
characters.who: THE POET'S PARENTS in 1990s winter clothes, seen arguing in the car at night (02) and in memory (09).

passage.line: Accepting you'll never say nor ever feel, my love was real.
passage.why_fulcrum: The acceptance turns his reach in the crowd into a farewell; every later scene (packing, calling mother and father, the EX turning to haze) is leaving, not pursuit.

answer.title: Mooch Goes to Hollywood
answer.said: I love you but I can't keep you.
answer.why: Another voice admits a real love that cannot be held, the same acceptance as his line, in plain words.
